editorial:
Captivity drops you into the dark world of a famous model named Jennifer who goes from magazine covers to a locked cell overnight. The movie wastes no time getting to the scary stuff, throwing you into a tense situation where Jennifer and another prisoner must survive a cruel captor's games. The vibe is grim and intense, with a focus on fear and survival rather than big action scenes. If you like tight, small-space thrillers, this one keeps things close and uncomfortable.

The acting is decent, with Elisha Cuthbert carrying most of the emotional weight as Jennifer. The pacing moves quickly enough to keep you watching, though some scenes feel repetitive. On the plus side, the tension stays high and the setting feels creepy. On the downside, the story can feel thin and the twists may not surprise everyone. This is best for horror fans who enjoy captivity thrillers and don't mind dark, heavy material. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Jennifer discovers that Gary, the fellow prisoner she trusted, is actually working with her captor Ben. Ben is obsessed with Jennifer and has been orchestrating everything. Jennifer fights back, killing Ben and escaping the chamber. Gary is left behind in the chaos. Jennifer survives and walks free, having turned the tables on her tormentors.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark captivity thrillers and survival horror.
